newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Garuda raises domestic cargo tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Garuda raises domestic cargo tariffs.

text.p: Indonesia's national airline Garuda said on Monday it had raised domestic cargo tariffs by up to 35 percent due to higher costs blamed mainly on a strengthening dollar.
Chandra Giri, head of Garuda's cargo division, said domestic cargo rates had been increased by 30-35 percent from December 1, depending on destination.
"Cargo tariffs have not risen from 1993 to 1996, whereas passenger fares have risen five times," he told Reuters.
"Our costs are based on the U.S. dollar and over the same period (1993-1996) the dollar has strengthened against the rupiah," he said.
The dollar was trading at 2,353 rupiah on Monday against an average 1993 dollar-rupiah exchange rate of 2,113.
Garuda had previously said it would raise tariffs by between 15 and 25 percent for domestic cargo and between 5 and 10 percent for international cargo.
Chandra said the airline would increase its international cargo rates early next year. He declined to give details.
He said costs had also increased in Garuda's domestic cargo operations since October when the airline launched its first cargo-only plane.
He said recent increases in the price of jet kerosene was another factor.
"We have two new freight carriers which we lease in U.S. dollars from Malaysia," Chandra said.
The first, a Boeing 737-200c, which serves domestic routes in eastern Indonesia from the country's second city of Surabaya, is leased from Malaysian Airline Systems Bhd.
"The second plane will operate from January and will be based in Jakarta and serve western Indonesia," Chandra said.
He said Garuda had also reached an agreement recently with Martinair of the Netherlands to operate an international cargo route between Jakarta and Amsterdam.
The route would be launched on December 17 and add to existing tie-ups with Korea Air and China Airlines, he said.
